title: Austin Infrastructure and City Services Spending
summary:
• **Storm Sewer Projects Approved** – The council allocated $1,723 for a new storm sewer on West 6th Street and $3 for lateral sewer connections on Congress Avenue to improve drainage infrastructure.

• **Pound Fee Refunds Granted** – Two residents (A.R. Boutwell and Mrs. C.M. McGee) successfully petitioned to have their animal pound fees refunded, though a third petition from Mrs. M.A. Taylor was referred to committee for further review.

• **Health Inspector Salary Denied** – The Finance Committee rejected a salary claim from H.W. Stroter, the Health Board Inspector, ruling he was never properly appointed and the Health Board had agreed to operate without paid positions.

• **Mayor Portraits Installation Ordered** – The council directed the City Engineer to restore and hang portraits of all former Austin mayors in the new council chamber.

• **City Clerk Books to Be Audited** – The council ordered an independent accountant to examine the City Clerk's financial records as soon as possible.

Austin, Texas, Sept 21 1908 :
To the Hon F M Maddox, Mayor, and Board of Aldermen of the City of Austin: Gentlemen: We
your Committee on Finance to whom was referred petition of H W Stroter for services
rendered as Inspector for the Health Board from July 1st 1908 beg leave to report that we
find no authority for the appointment and reappointment of Mr Stroter has not been
confirmed by the Council, as required by ordinance, and that there is no authority for
payment of such salary. The proceedings of the Council show that when the Health Board was
organized, it was with the distinct understanding that no salaries would be paid for this
department for the present fiscal year, and that no fee system would be allowed. We
therefore have to recommend that the petition be not granted.
R H L Haynes
